Emit only selected blocks. Be aware, that some blocks do depend on others, e.g. one can't emit `models` without emitting `enums`.  
Type: `("args" | "inputs" | "outputs" | "models" | "enums")[]`  
Default: `["args", "inputs", "outputs", "models", "enums"]`
- `omitModelsCount`
Omit `_count` field from models.  
Type: `boolean`  
Default: `false`

---
name: Pull Request
about: Multiple network requests on longer "Enter/Return" key press to improve backend performance.
---

## Description

Debounces network requests when a user presses and holds "Enter/Return" key on settings page while updating their name 
Fixes multiple network requests on longer "Enter/Return" key press to improve backend performance.

## Related Issue

Addresses #364

## Changes Made

This PR uses the existing implementation to debounce network request when a holds "Enter/Return" key while updating there name on `/settings/profile` route.

This creates a higher order function `updateUserDebounce(user,duration)`  to prevent multiple network request sent.

author: caioflp
body:
Eu passei algumas horas tentando decifrar o que estava provocando o seguinte erro de compilação:

> ./.out/trabalho-academico.toc|13 error| Argument of \MakeUppercase (arg 1) has an extra }.
> trabalho-academico.tex|| Runaway argument?
> ./.out/trabalho-academico.toc|13 error| Paragraph ended before \MakeUppercase (arg 1) was complete.
> ./.out/trabalho-academico.toc|13 error| LaTeX Error: The key '__kernel/\MT@gobble@to@nil \MT@nil' is unknown and is being ignored.

E aparentemente o pacote `microtype` causa esse erro na versão mais nova do `abntex2`, devido ao uso do commando `\MakeUppercase` na formatação do sumário. Veja, por exemplo [esta issue no repositório do abntex 2](https://github.com/abntex/abntex2/issues/259) ou [esta issue no repositório do microtype](https://github.com/schlcht/microtype/issues/29).

Aparentemente, este é um erro que não acontece sempre, sendo que um usuário relatou que ele ocorre localmente, mas não no Overleaf.

Tendo em vista que não conseguir solucionar o problema pode desmotivar alguém menos versado em LaTeX a utilizar este (muito bem adaptado, aliás) template de TCC para a EMAp, acho que vale a pena deixar esse pacote comentado, com um aviso para quem pensar em usá-lo.

author: hichamboushaba
body:
<!-- Remember about a good descriptive title. -->

Closes: #9787 Closes: #9788

### Description
This PR adds the following changes:
1. Feature flag for the project.
2. A new extension to check if the site is eligible for AI usage, this depends on the first part of the FluxC PR mentioned above.
3. A new property to check if a product is a sample product generated by WooExpress, this depends on the second part of the FluxC PR mentioned above.
4. A class that handles the navigation to the product creation flow, it will check the site's eligibility, then either show the AI flow or the regular flow.

### Testing instructions
##### Eligible WPCom site
1. Please use a new WPCom site, it has to be without products (excluding the auto-generated sample products)
2. Open the app.
3. Confirm that the task "Add product" in the onboarding list has the label of AI.
4. Click on the task, and confirm a Toast is shown (this is just a temporary thing to differentiate the AI flow).
5. Go back without saving the product, then go to the products list.
6. Click on the "Add" button.
7. Confirm the Toast is shown.
8. Create a new product and save it.
9. Go back to the products list, and click on the "Add" button.
10. Confirm the Toast is not shown anymore.

##### Eligible self-hosted site
1. Create a new site using Jurassic Ninja, and make sure the "Jetpack AI Assistant" option is enabled.
2. Connect the site to your WordPress.com account, then sign to the site in the app.
3. Repeat steps 3 to 10 from the above flow.

##### Non-eligible site
1. Sign in the app to a self-hosted site that doesn't have the "Jetpack AI Assistant" feature.
2. If the onboarding is still shown: confirm that the task "Add your first product" doesn't mention AI.
3. Go to the products list, and click on the "Add" button.
4. Confirm no Toast is shown.

- [x] I have considered if this change warrants user-facing release notes and have added them to `RELEASE-NOTES.txt` if necessary.

body:
This PR implements shallow hydration for Million.js **[Note: This is a big work in progress + is very messy]** ### Problem Currently, Million.js doesn't properly hydrate. Let's say that `` is a block component. ```js function Foo() { return } ``` If the SSRed HTML is: ```html
``` Then during hydration, React will hydrate the component: ```html
^ now has event listener
``` Then, on next re-render, Million.js will `replaceChild` the ` ``` This is effectively a destructive method to approaching hydration. ### Solution Instead of a full replace, we must reimplement the hydration from bottom up. This means, the vdom runtime, the react runtime, the react-server runtime and the compiler must be changed. ### PR Details **Status** - [x] Code changes have been tested against prettier, or there are no code changes - [x] I know how to update typings and have done so, or typings don't need updating **Semantic versioning classification:** - [x] This PR changes the codebase - [ ] This PR includes breaking changes (methods removed or renamed, parameters moved or removed) - [x] This PR changes the internal workings with no modifications to the external API (bug fixes, performance improvements) - [x] This PR **only** includes non-code changes, like changes to documentation, README, etc.

should be addressed to ensure that the component's CI testing is accurately

to this convention (i.e. you believe your component must be compiled with a Golang

architecture team and communicated to the ART team.

author: maisem
body:
Consumers of ipn.Notify (WatchIPNBus) need to be able to reconstruct the state of the world by just subscribing to changes after they ask for the InitialNetmap. This behavior was regressed when we made LocalBackend only handle a few types of mutations and not all; as the InitialNetmap sent down the WatchIPNBus may no longer contain all the up to date information and there was no way to recover the previously unhandled information.

This makes it so that the LocalBackend handles all mutations and panics if it sees an unknown type of mutation, and it also sends the mutations over the ipn.Notify bus.

Updates tailscale/corp#12990

body:
I had to disable `-Werror` in the default compiler settings for `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` to build with clang16, and I disliked that. So, I fixed all the showstoppers. None of them were critical, but overall, they increase readability, reduce probability of future bugs. The struct vs class fwd declaration *might* be problematic on MSVC, anyways, fixed that, no reason not to.

Also, moved the CMake version check in front of the project definition.

- CMake: Check for minimum version before setting the project name
- core/organisefmt: use same visibility for fwd decl as in def
- internet services: consistently use 'override'
- library: use boolean, not bitwise, operator on bools
- src: remove unused variable

author: manio143
body:
# PR Details

## Description

The Stride Profiler was a bit bloated with overloads and logic spread across different places. This PR addresses some of those issues by refactoring the base code. It also adds support for `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` to allow users to consume performance metrics outside of the game.

* Simplification of overloads by using nullable optional parameters
* Moving from longs to TimeSpans for improved typing of time data
* Addition of `ProfilingEventMessage` and modification of `ProfilingMessage` to make the logic of message formatting easier and separated from other concerns of the `ProfilingEvent`
* Move from `Dictionary<object, object>` to `TagList` which should be more efficient and easier on allocations
* Addition of `Meter("Stride.Profiler")` for external metrics consumption

Breaking changes in API
```diff
-profile.SetAttribute("MyAttribute", 5);
+profile.Attributes.Add("MyAttribute", 5);
```

## Related Issue

N/A

## Motivation and Context
I was exploring how to efficiently emit profiling data from a Stride game to existing tools for .NET that allow to measure performance. Initially I was exploring `EventSource` and `EventCounter` (the slightly older APIs) but they seemed less efficient to use directly, so in the end I used the [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/diagnostics/metrics).

As I was adding the support for those I saw a lot of complexity in the profiler code and decided to try to refactor it a bit.

We can now inspect the metrics using standard .NET tools
### dotnet-counters
```
dotnet counters monitor -p <pid> --counters Stride.Profiler
```
![image](https://github.com/stride3d/stride/assets/10709060/a261da2f-0d7f-430d-884c-65f169302c3d)

### Open Telemetry
```
var provider = Sdk.CreateMeterProviderBuilder()
  .AddMeter("Stride.Profiler")
  .AddAzureMonitorMetricExporter(o => o.ConnectionString = "")
  .Build();
```
![image](https://github.com/stride3d/stride/assets/10709060/f09a0027-b966-4290-9212-178ca1bf4c6f)

### Changes

  - webhookHandlerV2 only publishes messages to 2 topics now
    - Events from checker WhatsApp number result in messages published to "checkerEvents" topic

    - Events from user WhatsApp number result in messages published to "userEvents" topic 
- Added pubsub and pubsub emulators to project
- Created onUserPublish and onCheckerPublish handlers to replace the current webhookHandler's processing
  - Uses [cloud functions v2](https://firebase.google.com/docs/functions/2nd-gen-upgrade)
  - Functionally same as previously
- Turned OCR back on

### Issues Resolved
Resolves #122  
Resolves #152 

**Important Note:**
After prod deployment, go to https://console.cloud.google.com/cloudpubsub/subscription/list?project=checkmate-373101 and
- Change acknowledgement deadline to 120 for user and 60 for checker
- Activate Exponential Backoff
- Activate dead lettering and set max delivery attempts to 75, which will mean retrying for around 12 hrs

These cant be set within the function signature (see [this](https://dev.to/danielsc/firebase-function-retries-with-pubsub-3jf9))

Add companies details after new jobs have been scraped.

# Why
We want to be able to filter based on glassdoor ratings.

# How
The crawling process is run by Octoparse due to anti bot detection which make scraping from a script complicated. We feed this crawling process with generated companies urls that are not yet in the database. An ETL then adds them to Snowflake.

author: dimbleby
body:
switching from jsonschema to fastjsonschema, with the following intended advantages:

- jsonschema recently became not-pure-python, meaning that current versions are unsuitable for vendoring
- fastjsonschema has fewer dependencies, so that's less to vendor
- perhaps it's faster?!?

If I understand correctly it would even be possible to use fastjsonschema to [generate the schema-validation code](https://horejsek.github.io/python-fastjsonschema/#fastjsonschema.compile_to_code) ahead of time and ship that generated code instead of vendoring fastjsonschema itself.  That's what [setuptools seems to do](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/blob/2255e6366c70b9813d115ae0a0bba329affbd0ac/setuptools/config/_validate_pyproject/fastjsonschema_validations.py).  Maybe some other time.

Probably this will cause failures in the downstream `poetry` tests, let's get opinion on whether this is a good direction before starting the tedious compatibility dance.

author: blaggacao
body:
closes: https://github.com/frappe/frappe/issues/22438

# Context


https://github.com/frappe/frappe/commit/f4d0b0d35efa64a1692e075b71ae70c4969b81cda introduced the following regression:


```js
// parseFloat happens **not** to faithfully conserve the string value
parseFloat("12.030")
12.03
String(parseFloat(v)) == v)) == false

// parseFloat happens to faithfully conserve the string value
parseFloat("12.035")
12.035
String(parseFloat(v)) == v)) == true
```

If the string value is faithfully conserved, the parsing block is skipped.

In our case, that's the bad thing:

1. With the change of https://github.com/frappe/frappe/commit/f4d0b0d35efa64a1692e075b71ae70c4969b81cda, `parseFloat` may thus be invoked on the the raw string (in our example `"12.035"`) effectively returning 1/100th of that value (here `12,035`, a number!)
2. `_round` is then invoked on 1/100th of the actual value (`12.035`, a number!)
3. `_round`'s logic thus applies to 1/100th of the actual value
   - with a decimal precision of `0`, that will result in `12`.
   - that is awesomely wrong. QED.

# Proposed Solution

- [x] add test case and proof it fails ([link](https://cloud.cypress.io/projects/92odwv/runs/4f50994b-90a5-48e6-9f32-139e01c1fb77/test-results/c0dfa4ee-7ef6-4dc1-bb09-a8f51358814b/screenshots) showing a different symptom without having decimal precision set to `0` and thus is still proving point no 2 above)
- [x] revert the commit
- [ ] proof relevant test cases still work; findings:
    - The first commit's test resulted after the revert in:
      `Timed out retrying after 20000ms: expected '<input.input-with-feedback.form-control>' to have value '12.345', but the value was '12.345,000'` -> adapted the test in the 3rd commit together with more test coverage
    - after additional tests `control_float` [link](https://cloud.cypress.io/projects/92odwv/runs/35405/test-results?actions=%5B%5D&browsers=%5B%5D&groups=%5B%5D&isFlaky=%5B%5D&modificationDateRange=%7B%22startDate%22%3A%221970-01-01%22%2C%22endDate%22%3A%222038-01-19%22%7D&orderBy=EXECUTION_ORDER&oses=%5B%5D&specs=%5B%7B%22label%22%3A%22control_float.js%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22%5B%5C%225631a033-449f-499f-8eac-624606f6e76e%5C%22%5D%22%7D%5D&statuses=%5B%5D&testingTypesEnum=%5B%5D)
    - after additional tests `control_currency` [link](https://cloud.cypress.io/projects/92odwv/runs/35405/test-results?actions=%5B%5D&browsers=%5B%5D&groups=%5B%5D&isFlaky=%5B%5D&modificationDateRange=%7B%22startDate%22%3A%221970-01-01%22%2C%22endDate%22%3A%222038-01-19%22%7D&orderBy=EXECUTION_ORDER&oses=%5B%5D&specs=%5B%7B%22label%22%3A%22control_currency.js%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22%5B%5C%220452d0a1-743d-4b9c-800d-e290d5488da4%5C%22%5D%22%7D%5D&statuses=%5B%5D&testingTypesEnum=%5B%5D)
    - While this PR solves the original issue, the CI errors on [banker's rounding integration tests](https://cloud.cypress.io/projects/92odwv/runs/35405/test-results/b8230168-9cb7-4c56-9f0a-078053ba8553) even though I wasn't able to reproduce the failure locally (in my own environment) and even with these changes, banker's rounding continues to work as expected. (@ankush I might need some help with this, could be flaky or it is above my experience)


## Root Contributing Factors

I analyze that the root contributing factors to this happening are:
- Excessive functional impurity
- Lack of typing

<sub>If these patterns sound familiar, feel free to have a look at https://github.com/frappe/frappe/pull/21781, https://github.com/frappe/frappe/pull/21780 and https://github.com/frappe/frappe/pull/21779 which try to address _excessive functional impurity_ for the db backend.</sub>

author: rsheeter
body:
How might we understand what our threads are up to? - it's hard to tell from most profiles. By visualizing it ourselves of course! First hacky draft:

![image](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc/assets/6466432/63bf60dc-8a40-4d6f-9ffd-6fcf979ca5fb)

Above each row is a thread and time goes left to right. The pink area (color/label strategy tbd) shows very fine grained FE glyph work being distributed among threads, this is what we want. Next we see a period where nothing can be done until we have final glyph order, understandable but not what we want. We can see any speedup to glyph order production is a big win as it's delaying everything. Next we see a lot of per-glyph BE work in light blue, then a period where fea-rs is the long pole as we push toward completion. 

We can see that kern, which is executable as soon as glyph order is done and blocks backend fea, doesn't start for a quite a while which can work out poorly:

![image](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc/assets/6466432/2d39d870-7328-469f-b363-f90d29c2114d)

https://github.com/rayon-rs/rfcs/blob/master/accepted/rfc0001-scope-scheduling.md#current-behavior-per-thread-lifo suggests the order you submit to rayon can matter a lot. When I test with Oswald it seems kern is submitted with a large batch of backend glyph work and often sits in spot 600+ in the batch. If I hack to move it to the front it executes almost immediately after glyph order:

![image](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc/assets/6466432/b7b38a50-410c-4c19-bdc4-86be768770e5)

^ is significantly better; we will want to land some sort of prioritization. However, while this works for kern because it becomes executable at the same time as a large set of things that block on glyph order it doesn't work for fea so we still end up with fea not starting until all the be glyphs are done and then spending time as the only active task; if it had started as soon as kern finished we'd be in better shape:

![image](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc/assets/6466432/8f8dabb1-f174-46c9-9fc1-fde70e9bc4d4)

Plenty of room for refinement but already seems useful so I will try to prepare a less hacky version to land.

[GAME OBJECTS][GAME MODES][FEATURE]

## About the PR <!-- Describe the Pull Request here. What does it change? What other things could this impact? -->
This PR adds a new 1 TC traitor item, Reflective Glasses.

Reflective glasses act just like sunglasses, initially appearing as prescription glasses. They can have their appearance set once by using them in-hand, and they redirect flashes and flash cell assembly burning effects back at the flasher. Doesn't count area flashes, and it doesn't recurse if the attacker has reflective glasses too.

They can also be bought by Revheads. If someone tries to flash a Revhead wearing them, and they don't have eye protection themselves, they will be converted to a Revolutionary.

## Why's this needed? <!-- Describe why you think this should be added to the game. -->
This gives a defensive traitor option against a common stun option the crew has, while also being offensive and having some gimmicky-ness. Helps traitors and Revheads survive some more and gives them some resistance against being arrested.

While you can find sunglasses around the station, or use welding masks, this would be an available option that isn't hindering like welding masks and provides more utility than either.

Not sure if this is too similar to anything currently available for antagonists, defensive options like this aren't a traitor thing, or if this isn't a good solution for stun protection

## Changelog <!-- If necessary, put your changelog entry below. Otherwise, /please/ delete this entire section. -->
```changelog
(u)FlameArrow57
(*)Added a new 1 TC traitor item - Reflective Glasses. They reflect incoming flashes at attackers, and their appearance can be set once by using them in-hand. Also available for Revheads, where reflected flashes will convert attackers to Revolutionaries if they aren't wearing eye protection.
```

author: lahm86
body:
The main goal here is to get a step ahead of the next round of IO refactoring. The plan there is to have things such as models, entities and static meshes linked directly to type enums rather than using just numbers. This will eventually shift the specifics to the IO - so for example, `TR2Entity` has `TypeID` as a `short` but `TRModel` has it as a `uint` - these will become `TR2Type` in both cases and the necessary casting handled during IO instead of repeatedly throughout the solution.

Sorry this is another big one. It may be best going through commit-by-commit - here is a summary of the changes:

- Each game now has a complete type enum and namespaces for each changed to `TRLevelControl.Model` to avoid `using` bloat everywhere
- Explicit values have been assigned to each enum entry to make lookup easier
- The enums have been renamed from `TRXEntities` to `TRXType` - this makes the difference clear between `TRXEntity` and its type
- The type utility classes have been tidied up to match. No utility classes yet for 4/5 - this can be done when it's time to randomize those games
- TRGE DLLs updated as they make use of weapon types in each game

author: teswayze
body:
## Symmetry in endgame piece-square-tables

Following the use of separate tables for same-side vs opposite-side castling, the middlegame evaluation is invariant under reflection over the vertical axis (and would be negated if you rotated the board 180 degrees and flipped colors). With this change, the endgame evaluation will be consistent as well. Surprisingly, this change actually gained the most elo of anything here. The success of this change - and the failure of my Texel-tuned parameter update - will inform my evaluation tuning process going forward.

## Futility pruning at arbitrary depths

We now check if the current static evaluation beats beta by `128 * depth` at _every_ node. Previously we would only check if `depth<=2` and only do null move pruning otherwise.

## More aggressive time usage

This PR further cranks up the time used per move to a minimum of 1/40th of the remaining time (was previously 1/48th). This could potential further increase the frequency of timeouts related to #15, though I haven't observed that in practice.

## Evasion heuristic in move order

We now give a bonus to moves that evade a bad capture (such as a queen being captured by a knight). For now it's equal to the penalty for making moves that would allow the capture, though I plan to tune this in the future. For example we'd want queens to evade knights more aggressively than evading bishops as the bishop attack can be blocked.

## More conservative pruning of bad captures in quiescence search

I lowered the threshold on move priority used to detect whether a capture is searched.

## More aggressive late move reduction

We now reduce beyond the first 5 moves instead of the first 6. This has the most notable effect on node count and effective branching factor

author: howardwu
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting the PR! We appreciate you spending the time to work on these changes! -->

## Motivation

This PR updates the `cast` opcode to align with the new design for the `cast.lossy` opcode.

The implementation of `cast.lossy` under the hood has been updated to ensure there is no fallibility when converting between types, at the cost of lossy truncation. To ensure conversions from `field` to `group`/`address` are infallible, `Elligator2` is used as a fallback, when recovering from the x-coordinate is invalid.

In addition, the following changes are introduced:
- Adds `circuit::Address::zero()`
- Adds `circuit::Group::generator()`
- Adds `circuit::Integer::to_scalar()` and `console::Integer::to_scalar()`
- A benchmark for `Elligator2` is added to `console/algorithms/benches`.

## Testing

- Extensive unit tests are added to each casting operator for `cast_lossy` in `console`
- All unit tests in `circuit` for `cast` are updated with the new counts

## Reviewers' Note

The most important change worth a careful review is that of the `Field -> Group` `cast_lossy` implementation in `circuit/program/src/data/literal/cast_lossy/field.rs`. You should compare this against the `console` version to understand what the intended logic is supposed to be. (The `console` version is human-readable).

In addition, the impl of [`circuit::Group::from_xy_coordinates()`](https://github.com/AleoHQ/snarkVM/pull/1994/files#diff-e3592a499cc78d2ca1fb836e88e09d17f7f65720adab28ee78788a9f21174795) has been changed to prevent triggering a halting case. This logic should also be carefully reviewed.

author: jklina
body:
Howdy and thanks for the great library! 👋 I was looking into a way of adding an endpoint for monitoring metrics on job servers and saw that there was already an existing server used for health checks that uses the Rack interface. I did a quick spike that makes the health check server more general purpose and allows users to configure their own Rack apps for running on instances. Just wanted to get some input before pursuing it further and cleaning things up.

---
The health check and catchall logic are moved into simple Rack middleware that can be composed by users however they like and be used to preserve existing health check behavior while transitioning to a more general purpose utility server.

Additionally, this allows users to use WEBrick for the probe server in order to have a fully Rack compliant option.

All and all this pattern will allow users to add whatever functionality they like to GoodJob's web server by composing Rack apps and using GoodJob's configuration to pass in users' Rack apps. IE:

```
config.good_job.middleware = Rack::Builder.app do
  use GoodJob::Middleware::MyCustomMiddleware
  use GoodJob::Middleware::PrometheusExporter
  use GoodJob::Middleware::Healthcheck
  run GoodJob::Middleware::CatchAll
end
config.good_job.middleware_port = 7001
```

This could help resolve:

* https://github.com/bensheldon/good_job/issues/750
* https://github.com/bensheldon/good_job/issues/532

author: alnoki
body:
@davidiw @junkil-park @lightmark @movekevin @msmouse  @vgao1996

This PR adds storage account functionality, analogous to `malloc` in C.

Presently, global storage allocation can be done in one of several ways, which all have limitations:

1. Using a table requires expensive handle creation and hashing operations during lookup, and looking up data in the REST API is difficult with nested table handles.
2. Using a resource account requires the allocation of an `aptos_framework::account::Account`, which does not have a global resource group and thus leads to two global storage item creations during allocation.
3. Using an object requires creating an `aptos_framework::object::ObjectCore`, which can be incorporated in a resource group but which occupies almost 100 bytes. The `ObjectCore` can be deleted, but it requires several operations:
    - `object::create_object()`
    - `object::generate_signer()`
    - `move_to<ApplicationDataResource>` using the object account (AUID) signer, under the `ObjectGroup` resource group (to avoid having two global storage item creations)
    - `object::generate_delete_ref()`
    - `object::delete()`

Like during object creation, the proposed storage account functionality relies on an AUID, but is much more straightforward than the above process required for object-based storage allocation.

author: jamestkhan
body:
Discovered while working on game jam that the current approach in components to check isDirty, is not sufficient, as it entirely depends on the order of method executions. If getTransform() is called before the update of the Component, isDirty can be false by the time the component updates. In my use case CullableComponents OrientedBoundingBox was out of sync with the actual objects position as the isDirty() check was never true.

Now instead this bullet proofs the problem by adding DirtyObservable and DirtyListener, each SimpleNode/GameObject can have listeners subscribed to a onDirty event. 

Components (as applicable) now subscribe to this event so that they can perform translation updates when the parent GameObject is dirty.

Выполнено всё из секции Требования к репозиторию и как сабмитить задание [30]
Слайдер позиционируется с равными отступами слева и справа [10]
Соблюдено расположение картинок, подписей к ним и контролов [10]
Имеется плавная анимация смены картинок [20]
Имеется плавная анимация смены подписей к картинкам [10]
Подписи к картинкам должны быть строковыми значениями (текстом), т.е. текст не должен быть частью картинки [15]
Каждый контрол имеет большую область нажатия, чем размер самого контрола [5]
Контролы имеют интерактивность (момент наведения, момент нажатия, активный контрол, изменение курсора) [10]
Имеется мобильная версия слайдера, и соблюдено расположение картинок, подписей к ним и контролов [20]
Используются только относительные единицы измерения для основных блоков (картинки, контролы, подписи). Относительные единицы: rem, em, %, vh, vw, fr and etc... - присутствует "резиновость" слайдера [10]
Все блоки/составные части слайдера (контролы, картинки, подписи к слайдеру) находятся в базовом потоке дом-элементов, не позиционируются (position) с помощью top, left, right, bottom, не используется float. Можно: flex, grid, margin-left and etc... - все, что не упомянуто в запретах выше. Свойство position может быть только static. [5]
Не используются псевдоэлементы (не путать с псевдоклассами, псевдоклассы можно). [5]

Среди коммитов 6 оформлены согласно требованиям.

body: So, this is my second attempt at solving issue #2. The first time my workflow tests were failing due to node_modules overwriting issue. I created a second branch to take care of the node_modules folder and implement my changes. I first added a dropdown to the front end to choose a "type" for the post. This was done in composer.tpl in node_modules folder. I then captured the selected value of the dropdown in composer.js in node_modules again. This captured value was then sent to the back-end to assign the post object's attribute "type" with this captured data. This was done over multiple commits.

body:
This pull request introduces a checkbox which controls "Bold is bright" VTE option in Tilda (issue #325).

A new checkbox "Show bold text in bright colors" is placed in the UI below "Color Palette" section in "Colors" tab in configuration window. The placement and naming of the checkbox is inspired by similar option in `xfce4-terminal` and `Terminator` terminal emulators.

---

This pull request *should* also include an update of the translation files, but I'm unsure how to proceed with them. Current `.po` files seem outdated, and updating them automatically by running `make update-po` results in a huge change set (about 3700 modified lines). By examining Polish translation, I can see that some of the translations are getting "lost" (`gettext` moves them to the end of `.po` file and comments them out). That's happening for other languages as well.

I also tried updating the `po/POTFILES.in` file (because some of the strings that get commented out are located in files not referenced in this file). While this results in less "lost" translations, I can see that some of the strings are assigned incorrectly in Polish translation. I can only assume it is probably happening elsewhere as well.

If you find the code change acceptable, could you advise how to proceed with the translations?

4).Имеется плавная анимация смены картинок +
5).Имеется плавная анимация смены подписей к картинкам +
6).Подписи к картинкам должны быть строковыми значениями (текстом), т.е. текст не должен быть частью картинки +
7).Каждый контрол имеет большую область нажатия, чем размер самого контрола +
8).Контролы имеют интерактивность (момент наведения, момент нажатия, активный контрол, изменение курсора) +
9).Имеется мобильная версия слайдера, и соблюдено расположение картинок, подписей к ним и контролов ( немного обрезает картинку при 550) -
10).Используются только относительные единицы измерения для основных блоков (картинки, контролы, подписи). Относительные единицы: rem, em, %, vh, vw, fr and etc... - присутствует "резиновость" слайдера +
11).Все блоки/составные части слайдера (контролы, картинки, подписи к слайдеру) находятся в базовом потоке дом-элементов, не позиционируются (position) с помощью top, left, right, bottom, не используется float. Можно: flex, grid, margin-left and etc... - все, что не упомянуто в запретах выше. Свойство position может быть только static. +
12).Не используются псевдоэлементы (не путать с псевдоклассами, псевдоклассы можно). +
Смотрим от 1440 до 420px

author: jeqo
body:
Changes:
- Rename flag to disable certificate verification. from `aws.disable.cert.checking=false` to `aws.certificate.check.enabled=true`
- Adds configuration flag to disable checksum validation, and disables it by default.

See commits for details.

About disabling checksum:

We have observed that checksum validation adds ~20% more load when fetching logs. At the moment is not clear how to handle checksum issues; so this PR proposes to let Kafka handle any integrity when reading from a log. If this feature wants to be enabled, there is a new configuration to do this.

No checksum validation:

author: aimdexter
body:
## Key Changes and Enhancements:

1. Pagination with Atom Jotai Store: Integrated the Atom Jotai store into the project to manage the state and handle the pagination logic.

2. Data Slicing: To optimize performance and reduce the amount of data loaded at once, I have sliced the dataset into smaller chunks of 12 objects each. This ensures that only a manageable amount of data is displayed on each page.

3. Page Calculation: I have implemented a mechanism to calculate the total number of pages based on the size of the dataset and the number of objects per page. This dynamic calculation ensures that users always have an accurate overview of the available data pages.

4. Pagination Buttons: added pagination buttons, displaying page numbers and allowing users to navigate between different pages.

## Related Issues

Fixes #49

Please review and merge this PR. Thank you!

author: barnson
body:
Implements https://github.com/wixtoolset/issues/issues/7696.
Implements https://github.com/wixtoolset/issues/issues/7581.

`File` elements can appear where `Component` elements do in WiX v4. The
compiler generates an appropriate per-file component. Naked files under
`Directory`, `DirectoryRef`, `Fragment`, `StandardDirectory`, or
`Package` elements are included in a package via the [default-feature
feature](https://github.com/wixtoolset/issues/issues/7581). Naked files
appearing under `ComponentGroup`, `Feature`, `FeatureRef`, and
`FeatureGroup` generate the component and the reference to the parent
element.

This is a HUGE refactoring to switch from Redux to Zustand. The code is massively nicer, since we no longer need to pass around dispatchers. I also removed the "PTUI" object which I was passing around everywhere and using to access global state behind React's back (hey, this was my very first React project, after all).

Unfortunately, the typescript build isn't error-free, but I don't think this is related to my refactoring. Various things have changed in the typescript ecosystem in the past 6 years. I will probably need to do some more (less intensive) refactoring to get everything passing again.

## Description
This PR refactors the `messages` variable in the `ChatGPT` class in the `core/chat.py` file. The `messages` variable is currently a list of messages, and this PR migrates it to a new type called `Messages`. The `Messages` class is created in the `core/entities.py` file and behaves like a list, retaining all the functionalities of a list.

Additionally, this PR adds a new feature to the `Messages` class. The class now supports `with` statements, allowing for temporary swapping of system prompts. A new class, `PromptContext`, is returned by the `messages.prompt` function, which contains the implementation of `__enter__` and `__exit__` methods.

## Summary of Changes
- Created a new class called `Messages` in the `core/entities.py` file that behaves like a list. Implemented methods such as `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__delitem__`, `__len__`, `append`, `extend`, `insert`, `remove`, `pop`, `clear`, `index`, `count`, `sort`, `reverse`, and `copy`.
- Implemented the `__enter__` and `__exit__` methods in the `Messages` class to support `with` statements. The `__enter__` method swaps the system prompt with a new one, and the `__exit__` method reverts the system prompt back to the original.
- Refactored the `ChatGPT` class in the `core/chat.py` file to use the `Messages` class. Replaced the `messages` variable with an instance of the `Messages` class and updated all operations on the `messages` variable to use the methods of the `Messages` class.

Fixes #1658.

author: johnynek
body:
I wanted to try implementing cats.Eval now that we have polymorphic recursion #1041 .

I couldn't see a way to do it without a poor version of the fuel pattern: promise up front how many recursions you would do at most.

But along the way, I noticed that we are only returning one error message from any branch in the code in DefRecursionCheck, so I implemented a version of the idea in #1044 which allowed me to see all the error messages at once (when they are on parts of the code I was already traversing).

author: rcowsill
body:
(Work in Progress for issue #57)

This PR adds tooltips and links to the relevant run for all filled areas of the graph:

![image](https://github.com/jenkinsci/build-time-blame-plugin/assets/42620235/6eea605d-8067-45a0-bfde-d20a1d7b9ac7)

I found a couple of problems while working on this:
1. Coordinates in imagemaps aren't scaled to match the dimensions of the image they're used on. If the image is scaled down then the imagemap areas don't line up with the graph.
2. The default StackedAreaRenderer has a bug which omits half of each area from the imagemap.

The "trend graph" in Jenkins core avoids those problems by:
1. Making the graph fixed-size, which guarantees that the imagemap will always line up correctly
2. Using a custom renderer (StackedAreaRenderer2) which doesn't have the imagemap generation bug

The simplest approach (used by this PR) is to follow the example of Jenkins core, making the graph fixed-size and reusing their renderer. It does mean that the graph no longer scales down at smaller window sizes, and the graph appearance changes a little.

I tried out an alternative approach if those downsides are unacceptable. That would keep the existing graph appearance and image scaling, but requires some external .js ([davidjbradshaw/image-map-resizer](https://github.com/davidjbradshaw/image-map-resizer)).

### Testing done

* All tests pass (including new ones for the custom renderer methods)
* Manually tested graph tooltip and link functionality using `mvn hpi:run`

Para incluir FirePHP Core y habilitar la depuración en Moodle, puedes seguir estos pasos:

**Nota**: Antes de realizar cambios en la configuración de Moodle, asegúrate de estar familiarizado con la administración de tu entorno Moodle y de tener acceso adecuado como administrador del sitio.

1. **Instalar el Plugin FirePHP Core**:

- Accede al servidor donde se encuentra tu instalación de Moodle.
- Navega hasta el directorio raíz de tu sitio Moodle.
- Abre una terminal o sesión SSH en el servidor.
- Utiliza Composer para agregar FirePHP Core como una dependencia de desarrollo en tu proyecto. Ejecuta el siguiente comando:
  
     ```bash
     composer require --dev firephp/firephp-core
     ```

- Esto instalará FirePHP Core como una dependencia de desarrollo en tu proyecto Moodle.

2. **Habilitar la Depuración en Moodle**:

- Inicia sesión en el panel de administración de Moodle como administrador.
- Ve a "Administración del sitio" > "Desarrollo" > "Depuración".
- Asegúrate de que la opción "Activar depuración" esté habilitada.
- En "Configuración de mensajes de depuración", selecciona la opción "Desarrollador".
- Haz clic en "Guardar cambios".

3. **Configurar FirePHP Core**:

- Ve al directorio `vendor/firephp/firephp-core` dentro de tu instalación de Moodle.
- Copia el archivo `firephp-plugin.ini` a la raíz de tu sitio Moodle.
- Abre `firephp-plugin.ini` y ajusta la configuración según tus necesidades. Puedes configurar cosas como el nivel de depuración y la dirección IP permitida para ver los registros.

4. **Ver Logs en FirePHP**:

- Asegúrate de que tengas una extensión de navegador compatible con FirePHP, como Firebug para Firefox o FirePHP Extension para Chrome.
- Accede a tu sitio Moodle y realiza acciones que generen registros de depuración.
- Abre la consola de desarrollador de tu navegador y deberías ver los registros de FirePHP en la pestaña "FirePHP" o "Console".

Con estos pasos, habrás configurado FirePHP Core y habilitado la depuración en tu sitio Moodle. Ahora, podrás ver los registros de depuración en tiempo real mientras trabajas en el desarrollo y la depuración de tu plataforma Moodle. Asegúrate de deshabilitar la depuración cuando ya no la necesites, ya que puede generar registros significativos que pueden afectar el rendimiento.

author: thelastrar
body:
### Description of Changes
Remove HddSizeSectors setting and instead use the file size to calculate the number of sectors
Additionally, a crash fix to handle invalid LBA accesses.

### Rationale behind Changes
Previously it was possible to set size of the Hdd to a different value to the actual size.
Under such conditions we would report the set size, but report an error when trying to access beyond the end of the file.
This behaviour is unexpected and is pretty dumb.
Additionally, Some games (HDD Utility) would still attempt the read/write regardless of the reported failure, resulting in a emulator crash.

This change also makes it easier for a user to use their own dump, as we should no longer need to contend with GiB vs GB issues.

Unlike in Wx, the Qt build is only able to create a Hdd image in the settings UI, so we can remove the config field as well.

### Suggested Testing Steps
Test that Hdd images report the correct size.
Test that the UI works as expected.

`target` -> `Target`. Useful to users of machine-readable documentation.

When using the automatically generated documentation (in JSON format) in my application, I found two "Landing Target Estimator" param groups, with difference in "target" casing.

### Solution
- Change `target` to `Target` for consistency reasons.

### Alternatives
